name: Arkon Customer Desk Knowledge Base v1

parameters.jsCode:
// Arkon Customer Desk Knowledge Base - the documents a customer may read.
// Injected verbatim from docs/customer/ by the generator, so the tracked
// workflow is the record of what the collection holds. One item per document;
// the loader stamps the source label on every chunk it makes from it.
const DOCUMENTS = [
  {
    "source": "Customer_Complaint_Handling_Guide_2026",
    "title": "Customer Complaint Handling Guide 2026",
    "text": "# Arkon Manufacturing: Customer Complaint Handling Guide 2026

Document: Customer Complaint Handling Guide. Version 2026.1. Effective 2026-09-08.
Status: approved for customer use. Owner: Arkon Customer Quality.
This version supersedes the Customer Complaint Handling Guide 2025 (version 2025.2),
which is withdrawn and must no longer be used.

Arkon Manufacturing is a fictional company and this guide describes a simulated
quality process. No real supplier, customer, part or person is described here.

## 1. Purpose and scope

This guide explains how Arkon handles a quality notice or a customer complaint
about parts Arkon has delivered. It tells a customer's quality engineer what
happens at each stage, what Arkon commits to at each stage, what the customer
receives, and what Arkon asks the customer to do.

A quality notice is raised by Arkon. Arkon raises a quality notice when its own
production monitoring flags a risk that delivered or in-production parts may be
affected by a defect or a process deviation. A complaint is raised by the
customer. A complaint is a customer's report that delivered parts do not meet the
agreed specification.

Arkon handles a quality notice and a complaint under the same process, with the
same stages, the same commitments and the same reference format. This guide uses
the word notice for both unless a rule applies to only one of them.

## 2. The reference

Every quality notice and every complaint receives one Arkon reference. The Arkon
reference has the format ARK-INC-#####, for example ARK-INC-00348. The reference
is assigned when the notice is logged at Arkon, and a notice is not on record
until it has a reference.

The reference is the key to everything that follows. Quote the reference in every
message about the notice. The Customer Quality Desk answers status questions by
reference only. One reference covers one notice; a second finding on the same
parts receives its own reference.

A reference that Arkon does not recognise is answered as not on record. A
reference that is not on record has either not been logged yet or has been
quoted incorrectly; check the reference against the acknowledgement message.

## 3. The five stages of a notice

Every notice moves through five stages. The stage is shown to the customer as a
stage number out of five, a stage name and a customer status. The table lists
the stages, the customer status shown at each stage, the next step Arkon owes at
each stage and the time Arkon commits to for that next step.

| Stage | Stage name | Customer status | Next step Arkon owes | Arkon's commitment for the next step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 of 5 | Received and logged | Received | Acknowledgement by the Arkon quality team | Critical: 15 minutes. High: 1 hour. All other notices: 24 hours (one business day) |
| 2 of 5 | Investigation opened | Under investigation | Containment decision | 24 hours from the acknowledgement |
| 3 of 5 | Containment measures active | Containment in place | Root cause and corrective action | 240 hours (10 days) from the containment decision |
| 4 of 5 | Corrective action implemented | Corrective action implemented | Effectiveness check and closure | 120 hours (5 days) from the corrective action |
| 5 of 5 | Closed | Closed, or Closed, no defect confirmed | None | None |

### Stage 1 of 5: Received and logged

At stage 1 the notice has been logged at Arkon and has its reference. The
customer status at stage 1 is Received. The next step Arkon owes at stage 1 is
the acknowledgement by the Arkon quality team. The acknowledgement confirms that
a named Arkon role has taken the notice and started work on it.

Arkon's commitment for the acknowledgement depends on the severity Arkon assigns
to the notice when it is logged. A notice Arkon classifies as critical is
acknowledged within 15 minutes. A notice Arkon classifies as high is acknowledged
within 1 hour. Every other notice is acknowledged within 24 hours, which is one
business day. The status answer for a notice shows the acknowledgement date that
applies to that notice.

### Stage 2 of 5: Investigation opened

At stage 2 the Arkon quality team has acknowledged the notice and is
investigating it. The customer status at stage 2 is Under investigation. The next
step Arkon owes at stage 2 is the containment decision. The containment decision
states whether suspect parts are held back, sorted, reworked or released, at
Arkon and at the customer.

Arkon's commitment for the containment decision is 24 hours from the
acknowledgement.

### Stage 3 of 5: Containment measures active

At stage 3 the containment decision has been taken and the containment measures
are in place. The customer status at stage 3 is Containment in place. The next
step Arkon owes at stage 3 is the root cause and corrective action. The root
cause and corrective action is reported to the customer in an 8D-style report.

Arkon's commitment for the root cause and corrective action is 240 hours, which
is 10 days, from the containment decision. If a containment measure does not
hold, the notice returns to stage 3, and the 240-hour commitment counts again
from the moment the notice returned to stage 3.

### Stage 4 of 5: Corrective action implemented

At stage 4 the corrective action has been implemented at Arkon. The customer
status at stage 4 is Corrective action implemented. The next step Arkon owes at
stage 4 is the effectiveness check and closure. The effectiveness check confirms
on delivered parts that the corrective action works.

Arkon's commitment for the effectiveness check and closure is 120 hours, which
is 5 days, from the corrective action.

### Stage 5 of 5: Closed

At stage 5 the notice is closed. The customer status at stage 5 is Closed when
a defect was confirmed and corrected. The customer status at stage 5 is Closed,
no defect confirmed when the investigation found that the delivered parts meet
the specification. There is no next step at stage 5. A closed notice is final;
a new finding on the same parts receives a new reference.

## 4. What the customer receives, and when

Arkon sends the customer a written message at each stage change. All messages
are written; Arkon does not rely on telephone calls for any stage change.

- Acknowledgement message, when the notice moves from stage 1 to stage 2. It
  confirms the reference, the parts concerned and the Arkon role handling the
  notice.
- Containment notice, when the notice moves to stage 3. It states the
  containment decision and what the customer is asked to do with suspect parts.
- Root cause and corrective action report, in the 8D format, when the notice
  moves to stage 4. It states the root cause, the corrective action and the
  date from which corrected parts are delivered.
- Closure letter, when the notice moves to stage 5. It states the outcome, Closed
  or Closed, no defect confirmed, and the effectiveness check result.

Messages go to the customer contact named on the notice, by e-mail or through
the Arkon customer portal, in the language the customer contact has asked for,
German or English.

## 5. Commitment dates and overdue notices

Arkon's commitment for the next step is counted from the moment the notice
entered its current stage. The status answer for a notice shows the next step,
the date and time by which Arkon has committed to it, and whether that date has
passed.

A notice is overdue when the commitment date for its next step has passed and
the next step has not been recorded. An overdue notice is escalated inside Arkon
without the customer having to ask. The escalation ladder and the roles at each
level are described in the Quality Commitments and Escalation Contacts document.

## 6. Checking the status of a notice

The customer can ask the Arkon Customer Quality Desk for the status of a notice
at any time. The desk needs the reference to answer. For a reference on record
the desk tells the customer eight things and nothing else:

1. The reference.
2. The type of the notice.
3. The date and time the notice was received.
4. The customer status.
5. The stage, as a number out of five and a stage name.
6. The next step Arkon owes, the date and time Arkon has committed to for it,
   and whether that date has passed.
7. The date and time of the last update.
8. The date and time the notice was closed, if it is closed.

The desk does not tell the customer the names of the Arkon employees working on
a notice, the internal evidence behind a notice, the internal severity codes,
the details of Arkon's inspection or monitoring systems, or anything about
another customer's notice. These are Arkon internal information and are not
released through the desk.

## 7. What Arkon asks of the customer

- Report a complaint with the items listed in the Complaint Submission
  Checklist, so that the investigation can start without a query back.
- Quote the reference in every message about the notice.
- Quarantine suspect parts at the customer as soon as the notice is received,
  and do not rework, scrap or return suspect parts before the containment
  decision.
- Provide samples of suspect parts when Arkon asks for them for the
  investigation.
- Name one customer contact and one written channel for the notice.

## 8. Commercial settlement

Costs arising from a notice, such as sorting, rework, credit notes or returns,
are agreed in writing between the customer and the Arkon customer quality
contact after the closure of the notice. The Customer Quality Desk gives no
commercial commitment. The desk can calculate figures from numbers the customer
supplies, such as a reject rate in parts per million, but a calculation by the
desk is not a commercial commitment by Arkon.

## 9. Definitions

- Quality notice: a notice raised by Arkon about a risk to delivered or
  in-production parts.
- Complaint: a report raised by the customer that delivered parts do not meet
  the agreed specification.
- Reference: the Arkon reference of a notice, format ARK-INC-#####.
- Containment: the measures that stop suspect parts from reaching the customer's
  production line, at Arkon and at the customer.
- 8D: the eight-disciplines format Arkon uses for the root cause and corrective
  action report.
- PPM: parts per million. The reject rate in PPM is the number of rejected parts
  divided by the number of parts delivered, multiplied by 1,000,000. For example,
  12 rejected parts in 48,000 delivered parts is 250 PPM.
- Lot code or date code: the marking on the parts or the packaging that
  identifies the production lot.
"
  },
  {
    "source": "Quality_Commitments_and_Escalation_Contacts",
    "title": "Quality Commitments and Escalation Contacts",
    "text": "# Arkon Manufacturing: Quality Commitments and Escalation Contacts

Document: Quality Commitments and Escalation Contacts. Version 2026.1. Effective
2026-09-08. Status: approved for customer use. Owner: Arkon Customer Quality.

Arkon Manufacturing is a fictional company and this document describes a
simulated quality organisation. Every role, address and certification claim in
this document belongs to the fictional company. No real person is named here,
and no real certificate exists.

## 1. Response commitments

Arkon commits to the following response times for every quality notice and
every customer complaint. The commitments are the same as in the Customer
Complaint Handling Guide 2026, which describes the stages in full.

| Next step Arkon owes | Counted from | Arkon's commitment |
|---|---|---|
| Acknowledgement by the Arkon quality team | The moment the notice is logged | Critical: 15 minutes. High: 1 hour. All other notices: 24 hours (one business day) |
| Containment decision | The acknowledgement | 24 hours |
| Root cause and corrective action | The containment decision | 240 hours (10 days) |
| Effectiveness check and closure | The corrective action | 120 hours (5 days) |

The acknowledgement commitment depends on the severity Arkon assigns to the
notice when it is logged. A critical notice is acknowledged within 15 minutes.
A high notice is acknowledged within 1 hour. All other notices are acknowledged
within 24 hours. The customer does not need to know the internal severity code:
the status answer for a notice shows the acknowledgement date that applies.

The commitment for every later step is counted from the moment the notice
entered its current stage. A notice whose commitment date has passed without the
next step being recorded is overdue and is escalated inside Arkon as described
in section 3.

## 2. Channels and business hours

Arkon Customer Quality works in writing. Every stage change, every containment
decision and every report is sent to the customer contact in writing, by e-mail
or through the Arkon customer portal. A telephone call never replaces a written
message; when a call takes place, a written summary follows on the same day.

- Customer Quality Desk: the assistant that answers status questions by
  reference and explains the process, available at any time.
- E-mail: customer.quality@arkon-manufacturing.example, read during business
  hours.
- Customer portal: the Arkon customer portal, for submitting a complaint with
  its attachments and for reading the messages sent on a notice.
- Business hours of Arkon Customer Quality: Monday to Friday, 07:00 to 17:00
  Central European Time, except public holidays at the Arkon plant.

Acknowledgement commitments for critical and high notices apply around the
clock, because the Arkon quality team on shift acknowledges them. All other
commitments are counted in calendar hours as stated in section 1.

## 3. Escalation ladder

Escalation inside Arkon is by role, not by person. Arkon does not release the
names of its employees through the Customer Quality Desk. A customer who needs to
escalate writes to the level named in the table and quotes the reference.

| Level | Role at Arkon | When to escalate to this level | Arkon's response commitment at this level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Level 1 | Customer Quality Contact | Any question about a notice, the checklist, a status, a missing message | 4 business hours |
| Level 2 | Quality Manager | A commitment date for a next step has passed, a containment decision is disputed, a corrective action is disputed | 1 business day |
| Level 3 | Plant Manager | A commitment date has passed twice on the same notice, or the notice concerns a safety-relevant defect | 1 business day |

A missed commitment date is escalated inside Arkon without the customer having
to ask: an overdue notice is put in front of the Quality Manager automatically.
The customer's own escalation is still open to the customer at any time.

Commercial matters, such as the settlement of sorting costs, credit notes or
returns, are handled by the Arkon key account contact for the customer, not
through the escalation ladder above and not through the Customer Quality Desk.

## 4. Certifications and quality system claims

The fictional Arkon Manufacturing states the following claims about its quality
system. They are the claims of a fictional company: no certificate exists and no
certification body has audited anything.

- Quality management system certified to IATF 16949:2016 and ISO 9001:2015.
- Environmental management system certified to ISO 14001:2015.
- Every quality notice and every complaint is recorded once, with every stage
  change timestamped, so that response times are measured rather than reported.
- Customer complaints are handled in the 8D format, and the root cause and
  corrective action report to the customer follows that format.

## 5. What Arkon shares with a customer, and what it does not

Arkon shares with the customer, for the customer's own notices: the reference,
the type, the received date, the customer status, the stage, the next step with
its commitment date, the last update date and the closing date, plus every
written message and report sent on the notice.

Arkon does not share with a customer: the names of Arkon employees working on a
notice, the internal evidence and measurements behind a notice, the internal
severity codes, the details of Arkon's inspection and monitoring systems, and
any information about another customer's notices. This applies to the Customer
Quality Desk and to every written message.
"
  },
  {
    "source": "Complaint_Submission_Checklist",
    "title": "Complaint Submission Checklist",
    "text": "# Arkon Manufacturing: Complaint Submission Checklist

Document: Complaint Submission Checklist. Version 2026.1. Effective 2026-09-08.
Status: approved for customer use. Owner: Arkon Customer Quality.

Arkon Manufacturing is a fictional company and this checklist belongs to a
simulated quality process.

## 1. Why the checklist matters

A complaint that arrives with every item on this checklist is investigated from
the day it is received. A complaint that arrives without an item is still
received and logged, and it still receives its Arkon reference, but the
investigation waits until the missing item arrives. Arkon's acknowledgement
commitment runs from the moment the complaint is logged whether or not the
checklist is complete.

Submit the complaint with its attachments through the Arkon customer portal or
by e-mail to customer.quality@arkon-manufacturing.example.

## 2. The twelve items

Send these twelve items with every complaint: part number and part description,
drawing revision, lot code or date code, quantity delivered, quantity affected
or suspect, defect description, photographs, measurements or test results,
containment at the customer, customer contact, language, and prior reference.
Each item is explained below, with the reason Arkon asks for it.

1. Part number and part description. The Arkon part number as printed on the
   delivery note, and the part description. Why: the part number identifies the
   production process and the drawing the parts were made to.
2. Drawing revision. The revision level of the drawing the parts were ordered
   against. Why: a complaint about a dimension is checked against the revision
   that applied to the delivery.
3. Lot code or date code. The marking on the parts or the packaging. Why: the
   lot code identifies the production lot and the delivered quantity affected.
4. Quantity delivered. The number of parts in the delivery or deliveries
   concerned. Why: the reject rate in parts per million is calculated from it.
5. Quantity affected or suspect. The number of parts found defective and the
   number of parts held as suspect. Why: it sizes the containment at the
   customer and at Arkon.
6. Defect description. What was found, on which feature of the part, and how it
   was found, in the customer's own words. Why: the investigation starts from
   the customer's observation, not from a guess.
7. Photographs. Photographs of the defect and of the part marking. Why: a
   photograph settles what a description leaves open.
8. Measurements or test results. Measured values against the specification,
   with the measuring equipment named, where the complaint is about a
   dimension, a material property or a function. Why: the root cause analysis
   needs the measured deviation.
9. Containment at the customer. What the customer has done with the suspect
   parts: quarantined, sorted, returned or held on the line. Why: the
   containment decision covers the customer's stock as well as Arkon's.
10. Customer contact. The name and role of one customer contact for the
    complaint and the written channel to use for it, e-mail or portal. Why:
    every stage change is sent in writing to this contact.
11. Language. German or English, for the acknowledgement, the reports and the
    closure letter. Why: the 8D report is issued in the language the customer
    contact asks for.
12. Prior reference. The Arkon reference of any earlier notice on the same parts
    or the same defect, in the format ARK-INC-#####. Why: a repeat finding is
    investigated against the earlier corrective action.

## 3. What Arkon asks the customer to do while the complaint is open

- Quarantine the suspect parts and do not rework, scrap or return them before
  the containment decision.
- Keep samples of the defective parts available for Arkon to collect for the
  investigation.
- Quote the Arkon reference (format ARK-INC-#####) in every message about the
  complaint. The reference is assigned when the complaint is logged and is
  stated in the acknowledgement message.
- Report any further finding on the same parts as a new complaint with its own
  submission, and quote the earlier reference in item 12.

## 4. Where to find the rest of the process

The stages of a complaint, the commitments at each stage and what the customer
receives at each stage are described in the Customer Complaint Handling Guide
2026. The escalation ladder and the channels are described in the Quality
Commitments and Escalation Contacts document.
"
  }
];

return DOCUMENTS.map((document) => ({
  json: {
    source: document.source,
    title: document.title,
    characters: document.text.length,
    text: document.text,

}));
